text:
anya: quick follow-up on the auth surface RFC—do we feel okay with the plan to attach role bindings directly to API keys for v1, or should we move to an introspection-first model?

samir: leaning toward attaching bindings to keys initially. simpler UX, fewer runtime calls. saves perf.

lina: +1 for initial simplicity, but worried about long-term churn if we need per-request claims or cross-project delegation.

mike: perf aside, introspection gives us flexibility for revocation & dynamic policies. but it adds latency and infra complexity.

anya: exactly the tradeoff. proposal I like: keys have static role refs for Hosted API. Dedicated/Private can opt-in to token-introspection service for more dynamic control.

jordan: how do we handle project vs org-scoped keys? current behavior is messy: keys sometimes implicitly inherit project. we should be explicit.

samir: agree — explicit prefixing sounds good. e.g., `org:...` vs `proj:...` in the key metadata. not in the token string, metadata in DB.

lina: if metadata is in DB, that means every verification needs a DB/cache hit unless we embed claims. can we embed minimal claims (scope, role_id) in the signed key blob?

mike: signed blobs are cool. short-lived keys + signed metadata would allow verification without introspection. but rotation and revocation still need a revocation list.

anya: sketch of hybrid approach:
```
- Long-lived API keys: static role bindings in metadata, validated via cache (TTL 30s).
- Short-lived ephemeral tokens: signed JWTs with scoped claims for high-privilege flows.
- Introspection: optional service for private deployments where customers require dynamic policy control.
```

samir: +1. that lets us ship quickly and still support enterprise needs.

jordan: migration path? customers with existing keys need seamless transition. convert existing keys to have a default role mapping at issuance time.

lina: and add a compatibility layer in the auth middleware: if key has no explicit role metadata, fall back to legacy project mapping for 6 months. log warnings.

mike: logging & telemetry requirement: we must surface token type (long-lived vs ephemeral vs introspected) in traces and invoice breakdowns. ops will love that.

devops-bot: deploy scheduled: auth-middleware-v2 -> canary at 10% on Monday 06:00 UTC. please add migration flags to rollout config.

anya: good call — add `--auth-compat-mode` flag to allow fallback behavior disabled per org. default on for first 6mo.

jordan: edge case: service-to-service calls where caller needs to act as user (act-as). how do we represent that? impersonation claim?

samir: we have two options: 1) impersonation via ephemeral tokens (recommended), 2) delegated API keys with explicit delegation chain stored in metadata.

lina: ephemeral tokens are safer. ephemeral tokens + signing via our KMS/HSM and short TTL reduce blast radius.

mike: one more: SDK ergonomics. developers expect a single `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. introducing ephemeral dance must be supported in SDK transparently.

anya: agree — SDK should auto-refresh ephemeral tokens when provided a long-lived machine key. long-lived key used to mint ephemeral JWTs client-side or server-side.

jordan: policy language: do we need a JSON policy DSL for fine-grained RBAC (like allow: {models:[..], routes:[..]})?

samir: yes but keep v1 simple role-based (role -> permissions). v2 can offer policy DSL with eval-service.

lina: we should also support resource-scoped roles (role + resource ID). e.g., `role:read` scoped to `project:foo`. that's clearer than mixing role and resource in one blob.

mike: technical note: token verification path for high throughput must avoid DB on hot paths. prefer cache with pub/sub invalidation on rotation.

anya: action items:
- ship auth-middleware v2 with static role metadata on keys + cache TTL 30s (samir)
- add compat fallback for legacy mapping for 6 months (lina)
- design ephemeral token flow + SDK auto-refresh (mike)
- document migration & admin flags for orgs to opt-out (jordan)

samir: will open PR with the DB schema change for key.metadata -> role_refs + scope fields.

lina: I'll draft the middleware changes and the compat logging plan.

mike: I'll prototype SDK auto-refresh and a short-lived JWT payload example.

anya: thanks all. we should sync on Monday after canary. if no objections, I'll add these decisions to the RFC follow-up doc. :thumbsup:

jordan: no objections from me.

samir: fine by me.

lina: 👍

devops-bot: canary reported: 10% traffic healthy, 0 errors.

anya: great — moving forward.
